papers.title: Auditing Alignment Controllability in LLMs via Political Axes
papers.headline: LLMs easily steered across political spectrum by prompts alone
papers.blurb: A large-scale audit of seven LLMs finds system-prompt framing explains most political-response variance, far more than model identity, calling for new steerability audits.
papers.authors: Bartol Bućan, Nikola Sočec, Sarah Isufi et al.

papers.title: Test-Time Collective Action: Proxy-Based Perturbations for Correcting Algorithmic Harms
papers.headline: Users band together to fix AI bias without platform help
papers.blurb: Test-Time Collective Action lets user groups craft shared input perturbations via a proxy model to close accuracy gaps, no retraining or provider cooperation needed.
papers.authors: Meghana Bhange, Ulrich Aïvodji, Elliot Creager

papers.title: Manipulation-Proof Oblivious Audits Against Deceptive Model Providers
papers.headline: Oblivious audit protocol stops providers gaming fairness checks
papers.blurb: A private-information-retrieval-based audit protocol forces model providers to falsify far more responses to hide unfairness, increasing detectability without modifying the model.
papers.authors: Augustin Godinot, Sofiane Azogagh, Julien Ferry et al.

papers.title: Empirical Evidence and Analysis of a Critical Pitfall in Reward Learning from Human Feedback
papers.headline: Humans' wrong mental models distort feedback for reward learning
papers.blurb: A 211-person study shows human feedback reflects flawed internal dynamics models, a key limitation for RLHF-style methods across preference, correction, and off-switch feedback.
papers.authors: Taha Shaheen, Stephen G. West, Yu Zhang

papers.title: Toward Preference-aligned Large Language Models via Residual-based Model Steering
papers.headline: Steering vectors align LLMs without retraining or large data
papers.blurb: PaLRS extracts lightweight steering vectors from residual streams using as few as 100 preference pairs, matching DPO-level gains at much lower cost.
papers.authors: Lucio La Cava, Andrea Tagarelli

papers.title: An Agent-Based Simulation of Fairness Interventions in Hiring
papers.headline: Simulation shows hiring fixes differ in long-run effects on data
papers.blurb: A feedback-aware hiring simulation compares bias-mitigation strategies and finds that interventions with similar immediate outcomes shape future training data very differently.
papers.authors: Mattia Cerrato, Herbert Dawid, Stefan Kramer

papers.title: On the Generalizability of Fair Representations
papers.headline: Fair representations can work if classifiers are restricted
papers.blurb: Revisits impossibility results for fair representation learning, showing fairness guarantees become achievable when downstream classifiers meet accuracy or structural constraints.
papers.authors: Tosca Lechner, Shai Ben-David, Ruth Urner

papers.title: Fair and Representative Clustering for Data Summarization
papers.headline: New fairness measure for clustering goes beyond group counts
papers.blurb: Proposes a more expressive representativeness notion for data-summarization clustering and gives approximation algorithms with provable guarantees.
papers.authors: Ashwin Singh

papers.title: Algorithmic Gender Prediction Is Illegitimate, but Gender Imputation Can Yield Valid Measurements
papers.headline: Gender prediction can be harmful yet still measure real disparities
papers.blurb: Distinguishes legitimacy from validity in algorithmic gender imputation, arguing it can expose sexism against women while remaining harmful to trans and nonbinary people.
papers.authors: Evan Dong, Angelina Wang

papers.title: When Distrust in Humans Drives Trust in AI: Institutional Bias and Algorithmic Preference Among Marginalized Groups (Extended Abstract)
papers.headline: Marginalized groups prefer AI judges when human bias is visible
papers.blurb: Four experiments show people facing salient discrimination, especially minorities, shift preference toward AI over human decision-makers, raising concerns about masking inequity.
papers.authors: S Mo Jones-Jang, Rylee Ahn, Jiyoung Lee

papers.title: Enabling the 1:1 Promise: AI Enabled Fairness for Indonesia’s Retail IPO Allocation
papers.headline: AI network detects fake retail bidders in Indonesia's IPO quota
papers.blurb: A graph-and-ML framework identifies coordinated nominee accounts gaming Indonesia's retail IPO quota, cutting allocation inequality by over 60% in simulations.
papers.authors: Anchal Gupta, Gleb Papyshev, James T Kwok

papers.title: Epistemic Trustworthiness in Generative AI: A Normative Framework for Warranted Reliance in High-Stakes Workflows
papers.headline: New framework defines when trusting generative AI is justified
papers.blurb: Proposes three conditions—epistemic humility, access, and resistance to epistemic injustice—for warranted reliance on generative AI in high-stakes fields like law and medicine.
papers.authors: Nimisha Karnatak, Max Van Kleek, Nigel Shadbolt

papers.title: Lost in Translation: How Universal Ethical Values Fail to Translate Across Global Contexts
papers.headline: Experts worldwide reinterpret fairness and privacy to fit local norms
papers.blurb: Interviews with 14 experts across 10 countries reveal universal AI ethics values get reshaped by local conditions, exposing gaps in global governance frameworks.
papers.authors: Ozioma C. Oguine, Munachimso B. Oguine, Cesar Cervera et al.

papers.title: Connected EF1 Allocations Exist in Discrete Chore Cutting
papers.headline: Envy-free chore division proven possible with connected bundles
papers.blurb: Using the Simmons-Su topological framework, the paper proves EF1 connected allocations always exist for dividing a discrete chore, resolving an open problem for chores.
papers.authors: Ankang Sun, Bo Li

papers.title: Proportional Selection in Networks
papers.headline: Algorithms pick influential yet diverse nodes without group labels
papers.blurb: New algorithms select representative network nodes that balance influence and proportional diversity, using only connection structure, not explicit group data.
papers.authors: Georgios Papasotiropoulos, Oskar Skibski, Piotr Skowron et al.

papers.title: The Communication Complexity of Instant-Runoff Voting
papers.headline: Communication cost of instant-runoff voting pinned down exactly
papers.blurb: Resolves an open problem by proving IRV's communication complexity is Theta(n log^2 m), with tighter bounds under single-peaked preferences and for STV.
papers.authors: Élie de Panafieu, François Durand, Jérôme Lang

papers.title: Social Welfare Under Heterogeneous Time Preferences
papers.headline: Optimal group decisions get complex when agents discount time differently
papers.blurb: Studies welfare-optimal strategies in MDPs with multiple principals holding different discount factors, showing simple finite-memory solutions exist but threshold decisions are NP-hard.
papers.authors: Sarvin Bahmani, Soumyajit Paul, Sven Schewe et al.

papers.title: Voting Compilation Revisited
papers.headline: Theory pins down which vote-compression schemes work for which rules
papers.blurb: Fully characterizes which information structures can compactly represent voter profiles while preserving correct winner computation under future additional votes.
papers.authors: Yann Chevaleyre, Jérôme Lang, Nicolas Maudet

papers.title: The Alignment Problem Is an Identity Problem: Lessons from Four Billion Years of Major Evolutionary Transitions
papers.headline: Alignment reframed as identity, not just behavioral control
papers.blurb: A position paper argues AI alignment should focus on identity integration inspired by evolutionary transitions, not only external corrective constraints, with falsifiable predictions proposed.
papers.authors: Nyx Redondo

papers.title: Modeling and Explaining an Industrial Workforce Allocation Problem (Extended Abstract)
papers.headline: Constraint programming balances fair workloads in aircraft manufacturing
papers.blurb: An industrial case study models workforce scheduling with fair workload balancing and efficient rescheduling after disruptions like weather or equipment failure.
papers.authors: Ignace Bleukx, Ryma Boumazouza, Tias Guns et al.

papers.title: Exact Cut Complexity of Equal-Length Proportional Cake Cutting
papers.headline: Tight bound found for cutting cake into equal proportional shares
papers.blurb: The paper proves the exact worst-case number of cuts (2n-2) needed for equal-length proportional cake cutting and studies computability, improving on prior quadratic bounds.
papers.authors: Yasushi Kawase, Bodhayan Roy, Mohammad Azharuddin Sanpui
papers.venue: International Symposium on Mathematical Foundations of Computer Science

papers.title: Fairness Detectability: Do Explanations Recover Fairness-Relevant Causal Effects?
papers.headline: Causal explanations beat non-causal ones at revealing unfair effects
papers.blurb: The paper categorizes goals of fairness explainability and shows non-causal XAI methods systematically fail to recover fairness-relevant causal effects, proposing detectability measures to diagnose this.
papers.authors: Sakina Hansen, Kateryna Koval, Anna-Alina Bondarets et al.

papers.title: A Method for Learning Value Systems in Generative AI
papers.headline: New method learns layered value systems from chatbot preference data
papers.blurb: A value-learning algorithm infers both a multi-objective reward grounding and a weighted value system from pairwise preference data, improving explainability with minimal performance cost.
papers.authors: Andrés Holgado-Sánchez, Holger Billhardt, Sascha Ossowski

papers.title: Care-Full Alignment: Operationalizing Care Ethics for Human-LLM Relationships
papers.headline: Care ethics proposed as framework for safer human-chatbot relationships
papers.blurb: The paper operationalizes Tronto's care ethics into measurable indicators and tests whether care-informed DPO fine-tuning reduces harmful relational patterns in LLM companionship.
papers.authors: Rayane El Masri

papers.title: The Forager’s Dilemma: Peer Enforcement Alone Is Not Enough for Stable Multi-Agent Alignment
papers.headline: Peer punishment alone fails to keep multi-agent AI aligned
papers.blurb: A multi-agent simulation shows decentralized peer enforcement is vulnerable to free-riding, while combining intrinsic alignment priors with social enforcement yields more stable cooperation.
papers.authors: Majid Ghasemi, Prabhjyot Singh, Mark Crowley

papers.title: Fairness over Time: Evaluating How Fairness Objectives Shape Health Disparities in AI-Driven Clinical Decision Support Systems
papers.headline: Simulation shows fairness definitions can backfire over time in healthcare
papers.blurb: A Markov microsimulation compares five fairness-based allocation policies in chronic care, finding egalitarian and sufficientarian rules paradoxically worsen long-term disparities.
papers.authors: Kaitlyn E. Wade, Alice C. W. Huang, Daniel J. Lizotte

papers.title: Personalizing AI to Align with the Better You
papers.headline: AI assistants built to reflect your 'better self', not just your wants
papers.blurb: An LLM-driven interview pipeline elicits a reflective value profile across five dimensions to guide personalized AI behavior; a pilot study shows users find it authentic.
papers.authors: Jakob Stenseke, Jocelyn Zhu, Dylan Hadfield-Menell

papers.title: “How Much Do You Want to Play God in Controlling the Dataset?”: Data Scientists’ Perspectives on Modifying Data to Address Fairness Concerns
papers.headline: Data scientists reluctant to edit training data despite fairness concerns
papers.blurb: Interviews with 20 practitioners reveal that professional norms discourage directly modifying biased training data, even when fairness issues are evident, limiting fairness interventions.
papers.authors: Kevin Bryson, Galen Harrison, Margaret Jennings et al.

papers.title: Privacy Cost as Equity Input: A Group Fairness Criterion for Differentially Private Machine Learning
papers.headline: New metric treats privacy exposure itself as a fairness cost
papers.blurb: The Privacy-Cost Equity Ratio measures whether groups bearing greater privacy leakage under DP-SGD receive proportional benefit, revealing fairness gaps outcome-based metrics miss.
papers.authors: Rakshit Naidu

papers.title: Sources of Inequity and Fairness Risks in Wellbeing Sensing
papers.headline: Hidden inequities found across the lifecycle of wellbeing sensing systems
papers.blurb: Interviews with 14 practitioners identify situated sources of inequity in passive sensing beyond identity attributes, plus 15 fairness risks and mitigation strategies across the research lifecycle.
papers.authors: Han Zhang, Vedant Das Swain, Koustuv Saha et al.

papers.title: From Fair Representation to Just Recognition in Generative AI
papers.headline: Generative AI's representation problem reframed as misrecognition, not inaccuracy
papers.blurb: Drawing on Nancy Fraser's political theory, the paper argues generative AI's representational harms stem from failures of recognitional justice rather than mere descriptive inaccuracy.
papers.authors: Severin Engelmann, Daniel Susser

papers.title: When Interpretability Is Unequally Distributed: Fairness in Hybrid Interpretable Models
papers.headline: Hybrid interpretable models can route demographic groups unequally to black boxes
papers.blurb: The paper defines Interpretability Coverage Disparity to measure unequal routing to transparent versus black-box components, showing constraints can reduce this disparity cheaply.
papers.authors: Ziba Jabbar Zare, Ulrich Aïvodji, Julien Ferry et al.

papers.title: Spotting (and Missing) Algorithmic Bias: Investigating User Understanding in a Fairness Assessment Tool
papers.headline: HR users can spot algorithmic bias but overestimate their own understanding
papers.blurb: A study of 70 HR employees and job seekers using a co-designed fairness tool finds decent bias-identification accuracy but a gap between perceived and actual understanding.
papers.authors: Anna Verheyden, Yizhe Zhang, Robin De Croon et al.

papers.title: Beyond Stability: Improved Efficiency Guarantees for α-Stable Matchings
papers.headline: Relaxed stability rules unlock better welfare in matching markets
papers.blurb: The paper characterizes the tradeoff between α-stability and social welfare under asymmetric valuations, giving a polynomial algorithm achieving optimal efficiency guarantees.
papers.authors: Isabel Fernandez Abad, Sophie Klumper, Guido Schäfer

papers.title: Eliminating Envy in Multigraphs Through Subsidy
papers.headline: Half the subsidy needed to erase envy in graph-structured allocations
papers.blurb: The paper shows n/2 total subsidy suffices for envy-freeness in multigraph resource orientation, halving the general bound, with a matching tight lower bound and polynomial algorithm.
papers.authors: Bo Li, Ankang Sun, Shiji Xing

papers.title: Modeling Liquid Democracy: A Survey of the (Computational) Social Choice Literature
papers.headline: Survey charts the growing computational social choice literature on liquid democracy
papers.blurb: A systematic, taxonomy-based survey organizes modeling choices in liquid democracy research and outlines open directions for theory and practice.
papers.authors: Davide Grossi, Andreas Nitsche, Georgios Papasotiropoulos

papers.title: Computing Epistemtic EF1 and Pareto-Optimal Allocations of Indivisible Chores
papers.headline: Efficient algorithm computes fair and efficient chore allocations
papers.blurb: The paper gives a pseudo-polynomial algorithm for allocating indivisible chores satisfying epistemic EF1 and Pareto-optimality, advancing a previously non-constructive existence result.
papers.authors: Jugal Garg, Aniket Murhekar

papers.title: Fairness-Aware Optimization in Logistic Regression: Empirical Trade-Offs Across Healthcare and Socioeconomic Domains
papers.headline: Fairness fixes work better on big income data than small health data
papers.blurb: Tuning fairness regularization in logistic regression shows domain-dependent trade-offs, helping substantially on a large income dataset but little on a small heart disease dataset.
papers.authors: David Oluwabukunmi Shodipo, Blessing Ogbuokiri

papers.title: Understanding Fairness–Privacy Interactions in Graph Neural Networks: A Literature Review, Taxonomy, and Open Challenges
papers.headline: Survey maps how fairness and privacy collide in graph neural networks
papers.blurb: A review of 19 studies proposes a taxonomy of fairness-privacy interactions in GNNs, highlighting tradeoffs and open challenges for trustworthy graph learning.
papers.authors: Jingyan Zhang, Irina Tal

papers.title: Rules or Character? Scaling Laws for AI Safety Design (Extended Abstract)
papers.headline: Model suggests AI safety should lean more on character as scale grows
papers.blurb: A comparative-statics model of rules versus character-shaping in AI safety finds optimal resource allocation shifts toward character training at larger deployment scales, driven mainly by character fragility.
papers.authors: Satoshi Takahashi, Nobuji Kouno, Masaaki Komatsu et al.

papers.title: ABLEIST: Intersectional Disability Bias in LLM-Generated Hiring Scenarios
papers.headline: LLM hiring scenarios show compounding bias against disabled candidates
papers.blurb: An audit of six LLMs across 2,820 hiring scenarios introduces new ableism metrics and finds intersectional harms spike for disabled candidates marginalized by gender and caste in India.
papers.authors: Mahika Phutane, Hayoung Jung, Matthew Kim et al.

papers.title: People Are Not Just Their Countries. Disentangling Social Determinants of LLM Value Alignment Across Europe
papers.headline: LLM value alignment varies by education and income, not just country
papers.blurb: Analysis of 10 LLMs against European Social Survey data shows socio-demographic factors like education and religion explain alignment gaps as much as national identity.
papers.authors: Maria-Louisa Wightman, Guillaume Bied, Tijl De Bie

papers.title: From a River in Gilead to the Inference Distributions of Large Language Models: Covert Dialect Bias and Linguistic Profiling at Scale
papers.headline: LLMs show hidden dialect bias in housing judgments
papers.blurb: Probing internal probabilities across ten LLMs reveals AAVE and Nigerian Pidgin speakers are rated more negatively in housing contexts than Standard English, extending covert bias findings globally.
papers.authors: Chowdhury Mohammad Abdullah, Rita Orji

papers.title: Linguistic Triggers of Gender and Racial Bias in Open-Weight LLMs Applied to Recruitment
papers.headline: Job posting wording triggers gender and racial bias in hiring LLMs
papers.blurb: A multi-model audit finds agentic language hurts female candidates and coded-exclusion language suppresses non-White scores, informing an EU AI Act compliant audit protocol.
papers.authors: Kosuke Kitahara, Nobuhiro Yamaguchi

papers.title: Algorithmic Shortlisting in Participatory Budgeting
papers.headline: AI tools predict which budgeting proposals will win funding
papers.blurb: Researchers build and test algorithmic shortlisting methods for participatory budgeting, showing a vote-based pipeline lets LLMs match classical ML at predicting funded projects.
papers.authors: Juan Ignacio Zambrano, Clément Contet, Jairo Gudiño-Rosero et al.

papers.title: AI Alignment Without Representation: From Scalar Rewards to Social Deliberation
papers.headline: Proposal reframes RLHF failures as collapsed feedback signals
papers.blurb: The authors argue hallucination and moral drift stem from compressing plural values into scalar rewards, and propose Social RL with peer critique and sanctions to restore feedback integrity.
papers.authors: Majid Ghasemi, Mark Crowley

papers.title: Towards Fair and Accurate Short VAAs: Adaptive Ordering and Imputation in Democratic Recommendation Systems
papers.headline: Adaptive questionnaires improve fairness of short voting advice apps
papers.blurb: A new framework combining active learning and imputation personalizes voting advice app questions, boosting accuracy by over 12 points while exposing biases against minority parties.
papers.authors: Thilo I. Dieing, Lea Cohausz

papers.title: A Taxonomy of AI Value Alignment: Subproblems and Solutions
papers.headline: Value alignment is really several distinct unsolved problems
papers.blurb: The paper distinguishes subproblems like value identification, prioritization, and imperfect specification, arguing some demand technical fixes while others require ongoing ethical deliberation.
papers.authors: Daniel R. Harris, Karina Vold, Harsh Kumar et al.

papers.title: The Geography of Algorithmic Judgment: LLM Intermediaries, Place Identity, and Racial Steering in Housing Search
papers.headline: LLM housing assistants show inconsistent racial steering across cities
papers.blurb: A behavioral audit of seven LLMs across four US cities finds racial steering in housing recommendations varies by prompt context and city, challenging uniform fairness assumptions.
papers.authors: Hana Samad, Trung Lam, Christoph Mügge-Durum et al.

papers.title: AI Alignment and Fiduciary Obligation
papers.headline: Fiduciary duties proposed as framework for AI assistant alignment
papers.blurb: Drawing on business ethics, the paper argues developers owe users fiduciary duties of loyalty, care, good faith and candour, grounding alignment in developer obligations rather than values alone.
papers.authors: Benjamin Lange

papers.title: A Proxy-Based Method for Measuring Racial Disparities in Text-to-Image Generators
papers.headline: Legal-style proxy method audits racial bias in image generators
papers.blurb: Adapting antidiscrimination-law proxy variables, the study finds Imagen 4 Fast overrepresents white and lighter-skinned imagery compared to census benchmarks, unlike other models tested.
papers.authors: Nia Mucher, Ngan Pham, Jason Chin et al.

papers.title: What Drivers Want vs. What Drivers Take: A Worker-Centered View of Fairness in Ridehail Platforms
papers.headline: Ridehail drivers define fairness beyond simple pay metrics
papers.blurb: Interviews with nine drivers show fairness judgments combine location, duration, distance, and risk, revealing a gap between what drivers want and what algorithmic pressure makes them accept.
papers.authors: Samantha Dalal, Varun Nagaraj Rao, Christine Ao et al.

papers.title: Let’s Unlearn Stereotypes Before Decision-Making: The Impact of Intrinsic Bias Mitigation on Downstream Fairness in LLMs
papers.headline: Unlearning stereotypes in LLMs improves downstream decision fairness
papers.blurb: A new concept-unlearning method, FACU, reduces intrinsic LLM bias and shows measurable fairness gains in socio-economic decision tasks, especially combined with other debiasing techniques.
papers.authors: Mina Arzaghi, Alireza Dehghanpour Farashah, Florian Carichon et al.

papers.title: Protecting the Underrepresented: Data Debiasing via Asymmetric Adversarial Encoding for Fair Machine Learning
papers.headline: Asymmetric debiasing protects underrepresented groups in training data
papers.blurb: AdvEncoder aligns privileged group data toward the unprivileged group's latent space, achieving strong fairness-utility tradeoffs across four tabular benchmarks without heavy accuracy loss.
papers.authors: Deepanshu Aggarwal, Puspita Majumdar

papers.title: Asymptotically Fair and Truthful Allocation of Public Goods
papers.headline: New algorithm makes public goods allocation fair and truthful at scale
papers.blurb: PPGA uses differential privacy to achieve asymptotic truthfulness and core fairness for allocating divisible public goods, tested on real participatory budgeting data.
papers.authors: Pouya Kananian, Arnesh Sujanani, Seyed Majid Zahedi

papers.title: The Inherent Politics of AI as a Matter of Justice
papers.headline: Philosopher argues AI technology itself carries political bias
papers.blurb: The paper bridges formal and structural fairness debates by proposing that AI systems have 'justice-sensitive' inherent politics shaped by their technical characteristics, not just social context.
papers.authors: Laila Wegner

papers.title: Examining Racial and Gender Bias in CLIP via Explainability-Based Visual Attention Analysis
papers.headline: Attribution methods probe how CLIP's visual attention shows bias
papers.blurb: Applying four explainability techniques to a race-and-gender balanced occupation image dataset reveals race-conditioned saliency differences emerge mainly under explicit race prompting.
papers.authors: Tesnim Gülşen, Pınar Uluer

papers.title: Designing for the Intentional Stance: Stance Misalignment, Value Alignment, and the Case for Care Ethics in Human-LLM Relationships (Extended Abstract)
papers.headline: Care ethics proposed to fix emotional misalignment in chatbot relationships
papers.blurb: The paper diagnoses a 'stance misalignment' between developers' design view and users' emotional attachment to LLMs, proposing care-ethics-based alignment to address relational harms.
papers.authors: Rayane El Masri, Aaron Snoswell, Ehsan Dehghan

papers.title: Novel Applications of Large Language Models in Computational Social Choice
papers.headline: LLMs proposed to automatically design social choice algorithms
papers.blurb: This research agenda uses large language models to generate interpretable participatory budgeting rules and facility location mechanisms balancing fairness and strategyproofness.
papers.authors: Nguyen Thach

papers.title: Fairness and Stability in Allocation-Induced Hedonic Games
papers.headline: Fair allocation rules linked to stability in coalition games
papers.blurb: The paper connects fair cooperative-game payoff rules like the Shapley value to stability of induced hedonic coalition structures, bridging explainable AI methods with team formation theory.
papers.authors: Ayşe Mutlu Derya

papers.title: Tight Asymptotic Bounds for Fair Division with Externalities
papers.headline: Tight bounds found for fair division with externalities
papers.blurb: Shows envy can always be reduced to O(√n) items when agents care about others' allocations, matching a lower bound and refuting a prior conjecture about EF1 existence.
papers.authors: Frank Connor, Max Dupré la Tour, Vishnu V. Narayan et al.

papers.title: DiverValue-Bench: A Benchmark and Fine-Tuning Framework for Aligning Large Language Models with Diverse Human Values
papers.headline: New benchmark tests LLM value alignment across 74 countries
papers.blurb: DiverValue-Bench reveals hidden geographic and demographic disparities in LLM value alignment and shows lightweight fine-tuning with LoRA/DPO improves population-aware alignment.
papers.authors: Yao Liang, Dongcheng Zhao, Feifei Zhao et al.

papers.title: When Can We Trust Fairness Audits? Identifying Reliability Boundaries of Third-party Audit Conclusions
papers.headline: New metric tells when third-party fairness audits can be trusted
papers.blurb: Proposes 'Consistency Radius' to quantify how much a dataset used by auditors can diverge from deployment data before audit conclusions become unreliable.
papers.authors: Yuanhao Liu, Qi Cao, Huawei Shen

papers.title: The Price of Proportional Representation in Temporal Voting
papers.headline: Proportional representation in temporal voting costs little welfare long-term
papers.blurb: Quantifies the welfare loss from enforcing proportionality axioms over repeated collective decisions, showing JR's cost vanishes over time while stronger axioms remain costly, and proves related welfare maximization is NP-hard.
papers.authors: Nicholas Teh

papers.title: Quantifying Error Disparities in Population Health Models
papers.headline: Community health models show hidden accuracy-fairness tradeoffs
papers.blurb: A large-scale audit of county-level health prediction models finds adding demographic info boosts accuracy but often worsens error disparities, especially by income and education.
papers.authors: Aaron Marker, Salvatore Giorgi, Adithya V Ganesan et al.

papers.title: Uncovering Discriminatory Behavior in LLM-Based CV Screening Systems with Composite Statistical Metamorphic Relations
papers.headline: Metamorphic testing exposes bias in LLM resume-screening tools
papers.blurb: A legally grounded metamorphic test suite uncovers over 1,200 discriminatory failures across six LLM-based CV screening systems, with composite tests finding more defects.
papers.authors: Tetyana Turiy, Simon Speth, Alexander Pretschner

papers.title: Procedural Fairness in Machine Learning
papers.headline: Procedural fairness defined and measured for ML models
papers.blurb: Introduces formal individual and group definitions of procedural fairness in ML, a metric using feature attribution explanations, and methods to identify and fix unfair decision processes.
papers.authors: Ziming Wang, Changwu Huang, Ke Tang et al.

papers.title: Test-Time User Alignment via Bayesian Population Guidance in Subjective Tasks
papers.headline: Bayesian method personalizes model predictions from few feedback examples
papers.blurb: PGBC uses Bayesian calibration to adapt foundation model outputs to individual users in subjective tasks, outperforming zero-shot and in-context learning with minimal feedback.
papers.authors: Hoe Sung Ryu, June Christoph Kang, Christian Wallraven

papers.title: Multi-Agent Non-Discriminatory Contracts
papers.headline: Quantifying the cost of fair pay in multi-agent contracts
papers.blurb: Studies the tradeoff between maximizing a principal's utility and equalizing agent payments, proving a near-tight logarithmic 'price of non-discrimination' bound.
papers.authors: Ke Ding, Bo Li, Ankang Sun

papers.title: RM-Distiller: Exploiting Generative LLM for Reward Model Distillation
papers.headline: Reward model distillation exploits full capabilities of teacher LLMs
papers.blurb: RM-Distiller uses teacher LLMs' refinement, scoring, and generation abilities together, beating traditional binary-annotation distillation on reward modeling and RLHF benchmarks.
papers.authors: Hongli Zhou, Hui Huang, Wei Liu et al.

papers.title: Credit Fairness: Online Fairness in Shared Resource Pools
papers.headline: Credit fairness mechanism balances resource lending over time
papers.blurb: Introduces 'credit fairness' ensuring agents who share resources early can reclaim them later, showing it can't fully combine with both efficiency and strategyproofness.
papers.authors: Seyed Majid Zahedi, Rupert Freeman

papers.title: Beyond Client Clustering: Fine-Grained Preference Alignment in Federated RLHF via Self-Evolving Routing
papers.headline: Instance-level routing improves federated RLHF personalization
papers.blurb: FedPrism routes individual training samples to specialized experts rather than clustering whole clients, using self-supervised routing to better handle heterogeneous federated preference data.
papers.authors: Ke Wang, Shaojing Fu, Yuchuan Luo et al.

papers.title: Disentangled Graph-Enhanced Large Language Models for Fair Learning
papers.headline: Disentangled graph-text model reduces bias in LLM graph learning
papers.blurb: FairGEnt separates sensitive and sensitive-invariant information across graph and text modalities to curb bias amplification while improving LLM understanding of graph structure.
papers.authors: Zhipeng Yin, Zichong Wang, Zhong Chen et al.

papers.title: Fairly Dividing Non-identical Random Items: Just Sample or Match
papers.headline: Sampling few item values suffices for fast fair allocation
papers.blurb: Shows envy-free, welfare-maximizing allocations exist with high probability for non-identical random items, and can be computed fast by sampling only O(log m) values per item.
papers.authors: Aprup Kale, Navya Garg, Rucha Kulkarni

papers.title: A Survey on Value Alignment in Agentic AI Systems
papers.headline: Survey maps value alignment across agentic AI systems
papers.blurb: Proposes a multi-level value framework spanning universal, cultural, and context-specific values, reviewing alignment methods from LLM pretraining to multi-agent coordination.
papers.authors: Wei Zeng, Hengshu Zhu, Chuan Qin et al.

papers.title: BAMFair: Barycenter Aligned Mediation for Fairness Across Multiple Sensitive Attributes
papers.headline: Barycenter method scales fairness across many sensitive attributes
papers.blurb: BAMFair aligns subgroups to a global fair barycenter and mediates conflicting objectives via a Nash-based module, outperforming prior methods with multiple sensitive attributes.
papers.authors: Hengyu Yue, Fan Wang, Weiming Liu et al.

papers.title: Towards Fair Graph Learning Without Demographic Supervision
papers.headline: Fair graph learning achieved without any demographic data
papers.blurb: DIFGL enforces fairness by reducing treatment disparities among implicitly discovered subgroups, avoiding reliance on explicit or inferred demographic attributes.
papers.authors: Zichong Wang, Zhipeng Yin, Mo Sha et al.

papers.title: Learning Counterfactual Fairness from Authentic Generation
papers.headline: Counterfactual fairness improved via selective graph disentanglement
papers.blurb: GCFair identifies which graph features are genuinely affected by sensitive attributes, generating more realistic counterfactuals than methods assuming all features are affected.
papers.authors: Zichong Wang, Zhipeng Yin, Zhong Chen et al.

papers.title: Price of Fairness in Short-Term and Long-Term Algorithmic Selections
papers.headline: Static fairness rules can hurt long-term outcomes in selection
papers.blurb: Analyzes the 'Price of Fairness' in repeated selection, finding short-term fairness constraints can be costly while simple long-term investment policies shrink disparities cheaply.
papers.authors: Shahin Jabbari, Chen Wang

papers.title: Parameterized Approximation Schemes for Fair Clustering in Doubling Metrics
papers.headline: Fast near-optimal algorithms found for fair clustering in doubling metrics
papers.blurb: Develops the first fixed-parameter approximation schemes for group-fair and data-summarization-fair k-center problems by exploiting geometric structure of doubling metrics.
papers.authors: Xiaoliang Wu, Ting Liang, Zhize Li et al.

papers.title: Bounding the Fairness of a Classifier Using Population-level Statistics
papers.headline: Bounding classifier unfairness using only population statistics
papers.blurb: A new method lower-bounds a classifier's inaccuracy-unfairness discrepancy from aggregate rates alone, enabling audits without access to models or individual data.
papers.authors: Sivan Sabato, E. Yom-Tov

papers.title: Performative Castelessness or Ignorant Castefulness? Influence of Mahalanobis' Caste-Distance in Responsible AI Frameworks
papers.headline: Caste bias hidden in common fairness toolkits, study argues
papers.blurb: The paper traces the casteist and eugenicist roots of Mahalanobis distance used in AI Fairness 360 and critiques India's Responsible AI strategy for ignoring caste bias.
papers.authors: Nishanshi Shukla

papers.title: Beyond Base Metric: The Critical and Overlooked Role of Meta-Metrics in Intersectional Fairness
papers.headline: Meta-metric choices drive conflicting intersectional fairness verdicts
papers.blurb: The paper shows that how subgroup disparities are aggregated into a single fairness score strongly affects conclusions, proposing a taxonomy and guidelines for justified aggregation.
papers.authors: Jean-Baptiste Monnier, Thomas George, Frédéric Guyard et al.

papers.title: FairHireBench: A Cross-Generational Intersectional Bias Benchmark for Large Language Models in Automated Hiring
papers.headline: Intersectional bias amplifies 2.5x in LLM hiring decisions
papers.blurb: A benchmark of 10,000+ profiles across 15 intersectional groups finds large language models show significantly amplified discrimination beyond single-attribute bias.
papers.authors: Sweta J Ratnani, Ling-Yao Li, Yitian Lou et al.

papers.title: Diagnosing Algorithmic Bias: A Group Influence Framework for Fairness Auditing
papers.headline: Group influence functions diagnose roots of algorithmic bias
papers.blurb: Decomposing training influence into intra- and inter-group components reveals stereotyping and under-learning failure modes, enabling targeted bias mitigation on COMPAS and ADULT data.
papers.authors: O. J. Akintande, Amirreza Takhsha, Sune Holm et al.

papers.title: Learning Fairness in Multi-agent Systems with Distributed-Evaluation, Centralized-AIIocation
papers.headline: Reinforcement learning balances fairness and utility in resource allocation
papers.blurb: New Double Deep Q-Learning methods learn fair, efficient allocation policies in centralized multi-agent resource allocation, outperforming existing fair MARL approaches.
papers.authors: Ashwin Kumar, William Yeoh

papers.title: When Efficiency Shapes Fairness: Cost-Optimised Human-in-the-Loop Routing
papers.headline: Human review routing reshapes fairness without retraining models
papers.blurb: Studying deployment-time routing of cases to human review, the authors show risk-based routing reduces fairness violations better than uncertainty-based routing in credit decisions.
papers.authors: Veronica Breene, Adrian O'Hagan, F. Costello

papers.title: Options Without Agency: Diversity as a Requirement for Fair Actionable Recourse
papers.headline: Diverse counterfactuals needed for fair algorithmic recourse
papers.blurb: The paper argues existing recourse fairness metrics miss diversity of options, introducing a new metric showing diversity reveals fairness issues standard measures overlook.
papers.authors: Peter M. VanNostrand, Dennis M. Hofmann, Lei Ma et al.

papers.title: A Study on AI Readiness and Bias Risk in AI Based Recruitment Evidence from Selected IT Companies
papers.headline: Survey links AI readiness to bias risk in IT hiring
papers.blurb: A mixed-methods study of HR professionals finds that organizational AI readiness correlates with better management of bias risk in AI-based recruitment.
papers.authors: M.Pravallika Reddy, Thota Akhila, Thaya Madhavi et al.

papers.title: Ethical Principles for the Use of AI in the Military Domain
papers.headline: Ethical governance framework proposed for military AI
papers.blurb: The paper compares ISO/IEC and IEEE standards to propose a cross-sectoral governance framework for trustworthy military AI, including fairness and non-discrimination requirements.
papers.authors: Claudiu-Sorin Cleoanta

papers.title: Personalized Ballot Navigation Using Machine Learning for Visually Impaired Voters
papers.headline: Machine learning personalizes ballots for blind voters
papers.blurb: An adaptive ML interface for visually impaired voters cuts ballot completion time and errors in simulation, aiming to improve electoral accessibility.
papers.authors: Shat Mohammed Z.M.

papers.title: Fair Play: Exploring Play, Accessibility and Representation Towards a Framework for Fairness in Digital Games
papers.headline: Framework unites accessibility and representation as game fairness
papers.blurb: A new 'Fair Play' framework and card-based design tool frame accessibility, representation and play as interdependent dimensions of fairness in digital games.
papers.authors: V. Mota, Camila Laranjeira da Silva, Thaís Steinmüller et al.
